newsitem.title: USA: Ford's Hertz sees up to $480 million from offering.
newsitem.headline: Ford's Hertz sees up to $480 million from offering.

text.p: Car rental giant Hertz Corp., a unit of Ford Motor Co., said Thursday it expects to raise about $420 million to $480 million in its long-awaited initial public offering.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission in Washington, Hertz said it will offer up to 20.01 million shares at an estimated price of $21 to $24 a share. The offering represents about 18.6 percent of Hertz' total common equity.
Hertz will use proceeds of the offering to finance a $460 million dividend it paid to back to Ford on Feb. 27.

The offering, which follows an IPO in Ford's Associates First Capital Corp. finance unit last year, is aimed at unlocking the value of the automaker's assets for shareholders. The offering price implies that Hertz as a whole is worth up to $2.58 billion.

A Ford spokesman said the offering could take place by the end of March, following the completion of the registration period. Hertz shares will trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol HRZ.

Hertz, based in Park Ridge, N.J., said in the filing that the offering of up to 20.01 million shares includes a 2.6 million share overallotment option granted to underwriters, which are being led by J.P. Morgan & Co.

Although Ford chose J.P. Morgan over long-time investment bank Goldman Sachs & Co., as global coordinator, it included Goldman as a secondary underwriter for the deal. Others include Lehman Brothers Inc., Salomon Brothers Inc. and Smith Barney Inc.
Of the 17.4 million shares to be offered excluding the overallotment option, about 90 percent will be offered in the United States, and 10 percent will be offered overseas.
Ford, which will retain about 95.3 percent of the voting control over Hertz, intends to retain its remaining Hertz shares once the offering is complete, Hertz said in the filing.
Assuming that overallotment options are exercised, Ford will own 51.9 percent of Hertz' Class A shares and all of its Class B shares following the offering.
Hertz said it will pay an initial quarterly common stock dividend rate of 5 cents a share, which will be declared and paid during the third quarter of 1997.

The filing also said that prior to the $460 million dividend payment to Ford in February, Hertz' last dividend to its parent company was in 1995 for $25 million. Hertz paid no cash dividend to Ford in 1994 or 1996.
Hertz, which lays claim to being the world's largest car rental company, has posted record earnings for each of the past four years, earning $159 million in 1996, up 51 percent over 1995.
